usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind
connector_unbind() is the mirror of connector_bind(), but it is missing
the symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:

    if (port_dev->child)
        typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);

When a Thunderbolt dock is unplugged, two teardown paths race:

1. The component framework calls connector_unbind() first, which sets
   port_dev->connector = NULL without calling typec_deattach().  This
   leaves port->usb2_dev/port->usb3_dev in struct typec_port pointing at
   the USB device that is about to be freed.

2. usb_disconnect() then calls typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, ...),
   but port_dev->connector is already NULL, so the call is a no-op and
   port->usb2_dev is never cleared.

3. Concurrently, UCSI detects a PD partner-disconnect event and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which reads port->usb2_dev (now a dangling
   pointer to freed memory) and passes it to typec_partner_unlink_device()
   -> sysfs_remove_link() -> dev_name() on the freed device, corrupting
   the typec/UCSI partner state.

This corruption leaves the Thunderbolt tunnel in an inconsistent state on
the next dock hot-plug.  On affected hardware the dock's I225/igc NIC fails
to enumerate: AER fires a slot reset while the igc driver is still
initialising ("PCIe link lost"), and the subsequent igc_reset attempt hits
igc_rd32 on an already-detached device:

    igc 0000:2e:00.0 eth0: PCIe link lost, device now detached
    igc: Failed to read reg 0x0!
    WARNING: CPU: 9 PID: 129 at drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igc/igc_main.c:7005
             igc_rd32+0xa4/0xc0 [igc]
    Call Trace:
     igc_disable_pcie_master+0x16/0xa0 [igc]
     igc_reset_hw_base+0x14/0x170 [igc]
     igc_reset+0x63/0x110 [igc]
     igc_io_slot_reset+0x9e/0xd0 [igc]
     report_slot_reset+0x5d/0xc0
     pcie_do_recovery+0x209/0x400
     aer_isr_one_error_type+0x235/0x430
     aer_isr+0x4e/0x80
     irq_thread+0xf4/0x1f0

4. UCSI later handles the PD partner-disconnect and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which still sees the stale port->usb2_dev
   and tries to remove its sysfs link a second time:

   kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory
   WARNING: CPU: 6 PID: 55 at fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706 kernfs_remove_by_name_ns+0xe9/0xf0
   Workqueue: events ucsi_handle_connector_change [typec_ucsi]
   Call Trace:
    sysfs_remove_link+0x19/0x50
    typec_unregister_partner+0x6e/0x120 [typec]
    ucsi_unregister_partner+0x107/0x150 [typec_ucsi]
    ucsi_handle_connector_change+0x3ec/0x490 [typec_ucsi]
    process_one_work+0x18e/0x3e0
    worker_thread+0x2e3/0x420
    kthread+0x10a/0x230
    ret_from_fork+0x121/0x140
    ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30

   With worse timing the same stale pointer is dereferenced after the
   backing memory is freed, turning the warning into a use-after-free.

Fix the asymmetry: call typec_deattach() before clearing
port_dev->connector, matching what connector_bind() does on the bind side.
typec_partner_deattach() is already protected by port->partner_link_lock,
so it serialises safely with the concurrent typec_unregister_partner() path.

    the symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:
    
        if (port_dev->child)

    1. The component framework calls connector_unbind() first, which sets
       port_dev->connector = NULL without calling typec_deattach().  This
       leaves port->usb2_dev/port->usb3_dev in struct typec_port pointing at

       port->usb2_dev is never cleared.

       typec_unregister_partner(), which reads port->usb2_dev (now a dangling
       pointer to freed memory) and passes it to typec_partner_unlink_device()
       -> sysfs_remove_link() -> dev_name() on the freed device, corrupting
       the typec/UCSI partner state.

    the symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:

       port->usb2_dev is never cleared.

{

usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind
connector_unbind() is the mirror of connector_bind(), but it is missing
the symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:

    if (port_dev->child)
        typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);

When a Thunderbolt dock is unplugged, two teardown paths race:

1. The component framework calls connector_unbind() first, which sets
   port_dev->connector = NULL without calling typec_deattach().  This
   leaves port->usb2_dev/port->usb3_dev in struct typec_port pointing at
   the USB device that is about to be freed.

2. usb_disconnect() then calls typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, ...),
   but port_dev->connector is already NULL, so the call is a no-op and
   port->usb2_dev is never cleared.

3. Concurrently, UCSI detects a PD partner-disconnect event and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which reads port->usb2_dev (now a dangling
   pointer to freed memory) and passes it to typec_partner_unlink_device()
   -> sysfs_remove_link() -> dev_name() on the freed device, corrupting
   the typec/UCSI partner state.

This corruption leaves the Thunderbolt tunnel in an inconsistent state on
the next dock hot-plug.  On affected hardware the dock's I225/igc NIC fails
to enumerate: AER fires a slot reset while the igc driver is still
initialising ("PCIe link lost"), and the subsequent igc_reset attempt hits
igc_rd32 on an already-detached device:

    igc 0000:2e:00.0 eth0: PCIe link lost, device now detached
    igc: Failed to read reg 0x0!
    WARNING: CPU: 9 PID: 129 at drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igc/igc_main.c:7005
             igc_rd32+0xa4/0xc0 [igc]
    Call Trace:
     igc_disable_pcie_master+0x16/0xa0 [igc]
     igc_reset_hw_base+0x14/0x170 [igc]
     igc_reset+0x63/0x110 [igc]
     igc_io_slot_reset+0x9e/0xd0 [igc]
     report_slot_reset+0x5d/0xc0
     pcie_do_recovery+0x209/0x400
     aer_isr_one_error_type+0x235/0x430
     aer_isr+0x4e/0x80
     irq_thread+0xf4/0x1f0

4. UCSI later handles the PD partner-disconnect and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which still sees the stale port->usb2_dev
   and tries to remove its sysfs link a second time:

   kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory
   WARNING: CPU: 6 PID: 55 at fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706 kernfs_remove_by_name_ns+0xe9/0xf0
   Workqueue: events ucsi_handle_connector_change [typec_ucsi]
   Call Trace:
    sysfs_remove_link+0x19/0x50
    typec_unregister_partner+0x6e/0x120 [typec]
    ucsi_unregister_partner+0x107/0x150 [typec_ucsi]
    ucsi_handle_connector_change+0x3ec/0x490 [typec_ucsi]
    process_one_work+0x18e/0x3e0
    worker_thread+0x2e3/0x420
    kthread+0x10a/0x230
    ret_from_fork+0x121/0x140
    ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30

   With worse timing the same stale pointer is dereferenced after the
   backing memory is freed, turning the warning into a use-after-free.

Fix the asymmetry: call typec_deattach() before clearing
port_dev->connector, matching what connector_bind() does on the bind side.
typec_partner_deattach() is already protected by port->partner_link_lock,
so it serialises safely with the concurrent typec_unregister_partner() path.

content.text:
Root cause found. Here is the full chain, with evidence from this tree (`/workspace/linux`, HEAD = `028ef9c96e96` "Linux 7.0").

## Where the WARN comes from

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1730-1734` — the WARN fires only when `parent` (the kernfs dir of the kobject we are removing a link *from*) is NULL, i.e. the parent kobject has no sysfs directory anymore (already removed/freed):

```c
int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, const char *name, ...)
{
	if (!parent) {
		WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
		return -ENOENT;
	}
```
Called via `sysfs_remove_link()` → `fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143`.

The name being removed is literally `"typec"`, which is created/removed in exactly one place: `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:892` and `class.c:909`.

## Offending functions

1. `typec_partner_unlink_device()` — `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906-913`
```c
sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));   /* :908 — dev_name() of possibly-freed usb_device */
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");                 /* :909 — the WARN'ing call */
```
`dev` here is `port->usb2_dev` / `port->usb3_dev`.

2. `typec_unregister_partner()` — `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174-1196`, which unconditionally consumes those cached pointers:
```c
mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
if (port->usb2_dev) { typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev); port->usb2_dev = NULL; }  /* :1184-1187 */
if (port->usb3_dev) { typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev); port->usb3_dev = NULL; }  /* :1188-1191 */
device_unregister(&partner->dev);
```

3. UCSI caller: `ucsi_unregister_partner()` — `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138-1152`, `typec_unregister_partner(con->partner)` at `ucsi.c:1151`; reached from `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` at `ucsi.c:1325` (work item registered at `ucsi.c:1632`), matching "Workqueue: events ucsi_handle_connector_change".

4. The actual bug (missing teardown) — `connector_unbind()` in `drivers/usb/core/port.c:722-729`:
```c
static void connector_unbind(struct device *dev, struct device *connector, void *data)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;      /* :728 — no typec_deattach() ! */
}
```
It is *not* symmetric with `connector_bind()`, which does call `typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev)` at `drivers/usb/core/port.c:717`.

## Why ENOENT / "no directory"

- Type-C partner ↔ USB device links are cached in `struct typec_port` as `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev`, set in `typec_partner_attach()` (`class.c:2152-2158`).
- The only place that clears them on the USB side is `typec_partner_deattach()` (`class.c:2170-2186`), invoked through `typec_deattach()` (`include/linux/usb/typec.h:410`) from `usb_disconnect()` at `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2363`.
- On dock unplug the component framework runs `connector_unbind()` **first**; it sets `port_dev->connector = NULL` (`port.c:728`) without deattaching. Then `usb_disconnect()`'s `typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, ...)` (`hub.c:2363`) is a no-op because `con == NULL` (`typec.h:411`: `if (con && con->deattach)`).
- Result: `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` keep pointing at a USB device whose sysfs dir has been torn down (and whose memory is being freed).
- Later the UCSI worker handles the PD disconnect → `ucsi_unregister_partner()` (`ucsi.c:1151`) → `typec_unregister_partner()` (`class.c:1184`) → `typec_partner_unlink_device()` → `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` (`class.c:909`) on the stale kobject, whose `sd`/kernfs node is already gone ⇒ `parent == NULL` in `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` ⇒ WARN + `-ENOENT`. With worse timing it is a use-after-free (`dev_name(dev)` at `class.c:908`).

Note `partner_link_lock` (added by `ec27386de23a`) and pointer invalidation (`66e1a887273c`) only protect against *concurrent double unlink*, not against the pointer never being cleared — hence they don't fix this.
